proposals.before: The Ministry of Revenue drafted a plan noting that the imperial clan was expanding daily while its members depended entirely on state stipends—a major fiscal drain. It proposed reclassifying all descendants of the dynastic founder and earlier as jueluo, with each new jueluo generation subject to successive reductions in rank and allowance.
proposals.after: The Ministry of Revenue drafted a plan noting that the imperial clan was expanding daily while its members depended entirely on state stipends—a major fiscal drain. It proposed reclassifying all descendants of the Shizu Emperor and earlier as jueluo, with each new jueluo generation subject to successive reductions in rank and allowance.
proposals.reason: Chinese 世祖 is the temple name Emperor Shizu (Shunzhi), not a generic dynastic founder/Taizu.

proposals.before: The Ministry of Revenue drafted a proposal: imperial clansmen daily multiplied, and food and clothing all depended on official provision—a great drain on finances. It requested that from descendants of the Taizu on upward all be changed to jueluo status, and that those made jueluo be reduced in rank in succession.
proposals.after: The Ministry of Revenue drafted a proposal: imperial clansmen daily multiplied, and food and clothing all depended on official provision—a great drain on finances. It requested that from descendants of the Shizu on upward all be changed to jueluo status, and that those made jueluo be reduced in rank in succession.
proposals.reason: Literal wrongly renders 世祖 as Taizu; the temple name is Shizu.

proposals.before: Early in Daoguang he memorialized that Zhejiang's salt monopoly was poorly coordinated, proposing abolition of the salt commissioner's office, placing oversight under the governor-general, and a crackdown on smuggling together with abuses such as rule-bending, overweight charges, and illicit levies for supplies. The reforms were enacted as he proposed.
proposals.after: Early in Daoguang he memorialized that Zhejiang's salt monopoly was poorly coordinated, proposing abolition of the salt commissioner's office, placing oversight under the governor, and a crackdown on smuggling together with abuses such as rule-bending, overweight charges, and illicit levies for supplies. The reforms were enacted as he proposed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 巡撫 is provincial governor; governor-general would be 總督.

proposals.before: In the early Daoguang period he memorialized that Zhejiang salt administration lacked unified control, requesting abolition of the salt commissioner, return of management to the governor-general's concurrent charge, and orders to rectify suppression of smuggling and strictly forbid such abuses as skimming rules, overweight levies, and supply exactions; it was carried out as proposed.
proposals.after: In the early Daoguang period he memorialized that Zhejiang salt administration lacked unified control, requesting abolition of the salt commissioner, return of management to the governor's concurrent charge, and orders to rectify suppression of smuggling and strictly forbid such abuses as skimming rules, overweight levies, and supply exactions; it was carried out as proposed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 巡撫 is governor, not governor-general.

proposals.before: In his later years catastrophic floods struck repeatedly, above all in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and the lake provinces. Coming on the heels of the Western Region campaigns, the treasury was severely depleted.
proposals.after: Year after year there were great floods; Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and the lake provinces suffered especially often. Coming on the heels of the Western Region campaigns, the treasury was severely depleted.
proposals.reason: 瀕年 means successive/frequent years of flooding, not 'in his later years' of Wu Xiaoming's life.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Daoguang he was promoted to grand preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Daoguang he was promoted to Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: 詹事 is the Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, not grand preceptor (太傅/太子太師).

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Daoguang he was promoted to grand preceptor.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Daoguang he was promoted to Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: 詹事 should not be rendered as grand preceptor.

decisions.reason: s0069 has 世祖以上子孫; 世祖 is the temple name Shizu (Shunzhi), not the dynastic founder (太祖). Replacing 'dynastic founder' with 'the Shizu Emperor' corrects a real naming error.
The same unit writes 世祖, not 太祖. Rendering it as Taizu invents the wrong temple name; Shizu matches the Chinese.
s0091 says 歸巡撫兼理; 巡撫 is the provincial governor. Governor-general would be 總督, which is absent here.
Literal likewise mistranslates 巡撫 as governor-general; 'governor's concurrent charge' restores the office named in 歸巡撫兼理.
s0068 opens 瀕年大水: successive/recent years of flooding, not Wu Xiaoming's later life (晚年). The proposed 'Year after year there were great floods' matches 瀕年 and keeps 被災尤數.
s0025 has only 擢詹事. 詹事 is Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent; grand preceptor would be 太傅/太子太師, which the Chinese does not say.
The literal also renders 詹事 as grand preceptor. Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent is the correct office title for 詹事.
